---
title: "Fraudulent Clients"
format: html
execute: 
  eval: false
---

As discussed in the [Kaggle discussion](https://www.kaggle.com/c/ieee-fraud-detection/discussion/101203#589276) and highlighted in the [first-place solution](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/ieee-fraud-detection/writeups/fraudsquad-1st-place-solution-part-2), fraudulent activity may not be determined solely by the characteristics of an individual transaction. Instead, fraud patterns can also be related to the historical transaction behaviour of a given cardholder.

We therefore attempt to construct a proxy user identifier (`uid`) by combining several card-related attributes and the purchaser's email domain. We then aggregate the numerical variables within each group by calculating their means. This provides a user-level representation of the transaction data.

```{r}
#| label: unique-uid
train_by_uid <- train |> 
    mutate(uid = paste0(
       card1,
       card2,
       card3,
       card4,
       card5,
       card6,
       p_emaildomain
    )) |> 
    group_by(uid) |> 
    select(where(is.numeric), uid) |> 
    summarise(across(everything(), mean)) |> 
    select(-c(transaction_id, transaction_dt))
```

Finally, we remove variables used to construct the identifier, as well as other potentially identifying attributes, to obtain a more compact user-level dataset.

```{r}
#| label: remove-unwanted-variables
train_by_uid <- train_by_uid |> 
    select(-starts_with("card")) |> 
    select(-starts_with("addr")) |> 
    select(-starts_with("dist"))
```

```{r}
#| label: write-train-by-uid
write_csv(train_by_uid, file = "data-processed/train_by_uid.csv")
```
